source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ אֶל־לִבּ֔וֹ עַתָּ֛ה אֶסָּפֶ֥ה יוֹם־אֶחָ֖ד בְּיַד־שָׁא֑וּל אֵֽין־לִ֨י ט֜וֹב כִּ֣י הִמָּלֵ֥ט אִמָּלֵ֣ט׀אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֗ים וְנוֹאַ֨שׁ מִמֶּ֤נִּי שָׁאוּל֙ לְבַקְשֵׁ֤נִי עוֹד֙ בְּכָל־גְּב֣וּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְנִמְלַטְתִּ֖י מִיָּדֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said David to his heart, Now I will be swept away one day by [the] hand of Saul. There is nothing for me good but that I surely escape to [the] land of [the] Philistines, and will despair of me Saul, of seeking me again in all [the] territory of Israel, and I will escape from his hand.

en.L: And David said to his heart, "Now I will be swept away one day by the hand of Saul. There is nothing better for me than that I should surely escape to the land of the Philistines. Then Saul will despair of seeking me any longer in all the territory of Israel, and I will escape from his hand."
en.B: But David said to himself, "One of these days Saul will destroy me. The best thing for me is to escape quickly to the land of the Philistines. Then Saul will give up searching for me anywhere in Israel's territory, and I will be out of his reach."
en.R: But David thought to himself, "Someday Saul is going to kill me. The best thing I can do is to get away to the land of the Philistines. Then Saul will stop looking for me all over Israel, and I will be safe from him."

es.L: Y dijo David en su corazón: «Ahora un día seré destruido por la mano de Saúl. No hay nada mejor para mí que escapar enseguida a la tierra de los filisteos. Entonces Saúl desistirá de buscarme más por todo el territorio de Israel, y escaparé de su mano».
es.B: Pero David pensó: «Un día de estos Saúl acabará conmigo. Lo mejor que puedo hacer es escapar cuanto antes a la tierra de los filisteos. Así Saúl dejará de buscarme por todo el territorio de Israel, y yo quedaré fuera de su alcance».
es.R: Pero David pensó: «Algún día Saúl me va a matar. Lo mejor que puedo hacer es irme a la tierra de los filisteos. Así Saúl dejará de buscarme por todo Israel, y estaré a salvo de él».

fr.L: Et David dit en son cœur : « Maintenant, je périrai un jour par la main de Saül. Il n’y a rien de mieux pour moi que de m’échapper au plus vite au pays des Philistins. Alors Saül renoncera à me chercher encore dans tout le territoire d’Israël, et j’échapperai à sa main. »
fr.B: Mais David se dit : « Un de ces jours, Saül finira par me faire périr. Le mieux pour moi est de m’enfuir au plus vite au pays des Philistins. Alors Saül renoncera à me chercher dans tout le territoire d’Israël, et je serai hors de sa portée. »
fr.R: Mais David a pensé : « Un jour, Saül va me tuer. La meilleure chose à faire, c’est de partir au pays des Philistins. Alors Saül arrêtera de me chercher partout en Israël, et je serai à l’abri. »

vi.L: Đa-vít nói trong lòng: "Bây giờ một ngày nào đó ta sẽ bị diệt bởi tay Sau-lơ. Đối với ta không có gì tốt hơn là chắc chắn trốn sang xứ Phi-li-tin. Bấy giờ Sau-lơ sẽ thất vọng, không tìm ta trong khắp lãnh thổ Y-sơ-ra-ên nữa, và ta sẽ thoát khỏi tay ông ấy."
vi.B: Nhưng Đa-vít tự nhủ: "Một ngày nào đó Sau-lơ sẽ giết ta. Tốt nhất là ta mau trốn sang xứ Phi-li-tin. Bấy giờ Sau-lơ sẽ thôi lùng tìm ta khắp lãnh thổ Y-sơ-ra-ên, và ta sẽ thoát khỏi tay ông ấy."
vi.R: Nhưng Đa-vít nghĩ thầm: "Thế nào cũng có ngày Sau-lơ giết ta. Điều tốt nhất ta có thể làm là trốn sang xứ Phi-li-tin. Bấy giờ Sau-lơ sẽ thôi tìm ta khắp Y-sơ-ra-ên, và ta sẽ được an toàn."

decisions.choice: said to his heart: thought to himself
decisions.reason: To speak "to one's heart" is to say something inwardly, to think it over (Genesis 27:41). David is reasoning with himself; no one else hears him.

decisions.choice: swept away one day: destroyed some day
decisions.reason: The verb means to be swept away or brought to an end (12:25; 26:10). "One day" means at some time not yet known. Although Saul has just promised to do him no more harm (26:21, 25), David does not trust him.

decisions.choice: surely escape: escape without delay
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. David sees escape as his only safe course and means to do it at once and in earnest.

decisions.choice: despair of: give up hope of
decisions.reason: The verb means to lose hope and give up (Ecclesiastes 2:20). Once David is outside Israel's borders, Saul will see no point in hunting for him there.

decisions.choice: said to himself (Balanced); thought to himself (Readable); out of his reach / safe from him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the idioms of the heart and the hand into plain words. The hand stands for Saul's power to harm David, so "by the hand of Saul" becomes Saul as the one who acts.

source.text: וַיָּ֣קָם דָּוִ֔ד וַיַּעֲבֹ֣ר ה֔וּא וְשֵׁשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת אִ֖ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִמּ֑וֹ אֶל־אָכִ֥ישׁ בֶּן־מָע֖וֹךְ מֶ֥לֶךְ גַּֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And arose David and passed over, he and six hundred men who [were] with him, to Achish son of Maoch, king of Gath.

en.L: And David arose and passed over, he and the six hundred men who [were] with him, to Achish son of Maoch, king of Gath.
en.B: So David set out and went over with the six hundred men who were with him to Achish son of Maoch, king of Gath.
en.R: So David and his six hundred men left and went over to Achish, the son of Maoch. Achish was the king of the Philistine city of Gath.

es.L: Y se levantó David y pasó, él y los seiscientos hombres que [estaban] con él, a Aquis hijo de Maoc, rey de Gat.
es.B: Así que David se puso en marcha y se pasó, con los seiscientos hombres que estaban con él, a Aquis hijo de Maoc, rey de Gat.
es.R: Así que David y sus seiscientos hombres se fueron a vivir con Aquis, el hijo de Maoc. Aquis era el rey de la ciudad filistea de Gat.

fr.L: Et David se leva et passa, lui et les six cents hommes qui [étaient] avec lui, chez Akish, fils de Maok, roi de Gath.
fr.B: David partit donc et passa, avec les six cents hommes qui l’accompagnaient, chez Akish, fils de Maok, roi de Gath.
fr.R: Alors David et ses six cents hommes sont partis chez Akish, le fils de Maok. Akish était le roi de Gath, une ville des Philistins.

vi.L: Đa-vít đứng dậy đi qua, ông và sáu trăm người ở với ông, đến với A-kích con trai Ma-óc, vua Gát.
vi.B: Vậy Đa-vít lên đường, cùng sáu trăm người theo ông, đi sang A-kích con trai Ma-óc, vua Gát.
vi.R: Vậy Đa-vít và sáu trăm thuộc hạ lên đường đi sang A-kích con trai Ma-óc. A-kích là vua của Gát, một thành của người Phi-li-tin.

decisions.choice: Achish king of Gath: the king David fled to before
decisions.reason: David had gone to Achish once before, alone, and escaped only by pretending to be mad (21:11-16). Now he comes with an armed band and offers his service. Gath was one of the five chief Philistine cities (6:17) and Goliath's home (17:4).

decisions.choice: passed over: crossed over to the other side
decisions.reason: The verb means to cross over. David goes over from Israel to its enemy, a step that changes his standing in the story (29:3-4).

decisions.choice: six hundred men: David's band, grown from four hundred
decisions.reason: David first gathered about four hundred men (22:2); by 23:13 they numbered about six hundred. A band this size, with their families (verse 3), was a small fighting force.

decisions.choice: the Philistine city of Gath
decisions.reason: Readable reminds the reader that Gath was a Philistine city, as in 21:11, and gives the king's title its own sentence.

source.text: וַיֵּשֶׁב֩ דָּוִ֨ד עִם־אָכִ֥ישׁ בְּגַ֛ת ה֥וּא וַאֲנָשָׁ֖יו אִ֣ישׁ וּבֵית֑וֹ דָּוִד֙ וּשְׁתֵּ֣י נָשָׁ֔יו אֲחִינֹ֨עַם֙ הַיִּזְרְעֵאלִ֔ית וַאֲבִיגַ֥יִל אֵֽשֶׁת־נָבָ֖ל הַֽכַּרְמְלִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: And dwelt David with Achish in Gath, he and his men, each and his household, David and two his wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail [the] wife of Nabal, the Carmelite.

en.L: And David dwelt with Achish in Gath, he and his men, each [with] his household, David and his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail the wife of Nabal, the Carmelite.
en.B: David and his men settled with Achish in Gath, each man with his household. David had his two wives with him, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail of Carmel, Nabal's widow.
en.R: David and his men lived in Gath with Achish, and each man had his family with him. David's two wives were with him too. They were Ahinoam from the town of Jezreel and Abigail from Carmel, who had been Nabal's wife.

es.L: Y habitó David con Aquis en Gat, él y sus hombres, cada uno con su familia, David y sus dos mujeres, Ahinoam la jezreelita y Abigail, la mujer de Nabal, la de Carmel.
es.B: David y sus hombres se establecieron en Gat con Aquis, cada uno con su familia. David tenía consigo a sus dos esposas, Ahinoam de Jezreel y Abigail de Carmel, la viuda de Nabal.
es.R: David y sus hombres vivieron en Gat con Aquis, y cada hombre tenía a su familia con él. Las dos esposas de David también estaban con él. Eran Ahinoam, del pueblo de Jezreel, y Abigail, de Carmel, que había sido la esposa de Nabal.

fr.L: Et David habita avec Akish à Gath, lui et ses hommes, chacun avec sa maison, David et ses deux femmes, Ahinoam la Jizreélite et Abigaïl, la femme de Nabal, la Carmélite.
fr.B: David et ses hommes s’établirent chez Akish à Gath, chacun avec sa famille. David avait avec lui ses deux femmes, Ahinoam de Jizreël et Abigaïl de Carmel, la veuve de Nabal.
fr.R: David et ses hommes ont habité à Gath avec Akish, et chaque homme avait sa famille avec lui. Les deux femmes de David étaient avec lui elles aussi : Ahinoam, de la ville de Jizreël, et Abigaïl, de Carmel, qui avait été la femme de Nabal.

vi.L: Đa-vít ở với A-kích tại Gát, ông và những người của ông, mỗi người với gia đình mình; Đa-vít với hai vợ, A-hi-nô-am người Gít-rê-ên và A-bi-ga-in người Cạt-mên, vợ của Na-banh.
vi.B: Đa-vít và thuộc hạ định cư với A-kích tại Gát, mỗi người cùng với gia đình mình. Đa-vít có hai vợ đi theo: A-hi-nô-am người Gít-rê-ên và A-bi-ga-in người Cạt-mên, vợ góa của Na-banh.
vi.R: Đa-vít và thuộc hạ sống với A-kích tại Gát, mỗi người đều có gia đình đi theo. Hai vợ của Đa-vít cũng ở với ông. Đó là A-hi-nô-am ở thành Gít-rê-ên và A-bi-ga-in ở Cạt-mên, vợ trước đây của Na-banh.

decisions.choice: each with his household: whole families moved
decisions.reason: The men brought their wives and children with them (30:3). David's band was settling in Philistine land, not making a short raid.

decisions.choice: Ahinoam and Abigail: the wives David married in chapter 25
decisions.reason: David married Abigail after Nabal's death and also took Ahinoam of Jezreel (25:39-43). Jezreel here is probably the town in the hill country of Judah (Joshua 15:56), not the better-known Jezreel in the north.

decisions.choice: the Carmelite: the woman from Carmel, that is, Abigail
decisions.reason: The word "Carmelite" has a feminine form, so it describes Abigail, not Nabal. Carmel was the town in Judah where Nabal kept his flocks (25:2). "Wife of Nabal" names her by her late husband, so she is his widow (25:39).

decisions.choice: of Carmel, Nabal's widow (Balanced); from Carmel, who had been Nabal's wife (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the wife of Nabal". Since Nabal had died, Balanced says "widow" and Readable says she "had been" his wife. Both attach "Carmel" to Abigail, as the Hebrew does.

source.text: וַיֻּגַּ֣ד לְשָׁא֔וּל כִּֽי־בָרַ֥ח דָּוִ֖ד גַּ֑ת וְלֹֽא־יָסַ֥ף ע֖וֹד לְבַקְשֽׁוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And it was told to Saul that had fled David [to] Gath, and not he again continued to seek him.

en.L: And it was told to Saul that David had fled [to] Gath, and he did not again seek him any longer.
en.B: When word reached Saul that David had fled to Gath, he stopped searching for him.
en.R: Someone told Saul that David had run away to Gath. So Saul stopped looking for him.

es.L: Y se le informó a Saúl que David había huido a Gat, y no volvió a buscarlo más.
es.B: Cuando Saúl supo que David había huido a Gat, dejó de buscarlo.
es.R: Alguien le contó a Saúl que David se había escapado a Gat. Así que Saúl dejó de buscarlo.

fr.L: Et on rapporta à Saül que David s’était enfui à Gath, et il ne continua plus à le chercher.
fr.B: Quand Saül apprit que David s’était enfui à Gath, il cessa de le rechercher.
fr.R: Quelqu’un a dit à Saül que David s’était enfui à Gath. Alors Saül a arrêté de le chercher.

vi.L: Người ta báo cho Sau-lơ rằng Đa-vít đã trốn [đến] Gát, và ông không tìm Đa-vít nữa.
vi.B: Khi Sau-lơ được tin Đa-vít đã trốn đến Gát, ông thôi lùng tìm Đa-vít.
vi.R: Có người báo cho Sau-lơ biết Đa-vít đã trốn sang Gát. Vì vậy Sau-lơ thôi tìm ông.

decisions.choice: no longer sought him: David's reasoning proves right
decisions.reason: What David expected in verse 1 comes about: once David is outside Israel, Saul stops hunting him. The words echo verse 1 ("seeking me any longer").

decisions.choice: he continued: the reading noted in the margin
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text spell the verb in a slightly different form, and the reading noted by the scribes in the margin gives the usual form. The meaning is the same either way.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶל־אָכִ֗ישׁ אִם־נָא֩ מָצָ֨אתִי חֵ֤ן בְּעֵינֶ֨יךָ֙ יִתְּנוּ־לִ֣י מָק֗וֹם בְּאַחַ֛ת עָרֵ֥י הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה וְאֵ֣שְׁבָה שָּׁ֑ם וְלָ֨מָּה יֵשֵׁ֧ב עַבְדְּךָ֛ בְּעִ֥יר הַמַּמְלָכָ֖ה עִמָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said David to Achish, If please I have found favor in your eyes, let them give to me a place in one [of the] towns of the field, and I will dwell there. And why should dwell your servant in [the] city of the kingdom with you?

en.L: And David said to Achish, "If, please, I have found favor in your eyes, let them give me a place in one of the towns of the countryside, and I will dwell there. For why should your servant dwell in the royal city with you?"
en.B: Then David said to Achish, "If I have found favor with you, please let me be given a place in one of the country towns, so that I can live there. Why should your servant live in the royal city with you?"
en.R: Then David said to Achish, "If you are pleased with me, please give me a place in one of the towns out in the country. I can live there. There is no need for me to live with you in the king's city."

es.L: Y dijo David a Aquis: «Si, te ruego, he hallado gracia ante tus ojos, que me den un lugar en una de las ciudades del campo, y habitaré allí. ¿Pues por qué ha de habitar tu siervo contigo en la ciudad real?».
es.B: Después David le dijo a Aquis: «Si me he ganado tu favor, te ruego que me den un lugar en uno de los pueblos del campo para vivir allí. ¿Por qué ha de vivir tu siervo contigo en la ciudad real?».
es.R: Después David le dijo a Aquis: «Si estás contento conmigo, por favor, dame un lugar en uno de los pueblos del campo. Yo puedo vivir allí. No hace falta que viva contigo en la ciudad del rey».

fr.L: Et David dit à Akish : « Si, je te prie, j’ai trouvé grâce à tes yeux, qu’on me donne une place dans l’une des villes de la campagne, et j’y habiterai. Car pourquoi ton serviteur habiterait-il avec toi dans la ville royale ? »
fr.B: Puis David dit à Akish : « Si j’ai trouvé grâce à tes yeux, qu’on me donne, je te prie, un endroit dans l’une des villes de la campagne pour que je puisse y vivre. Pourquoi ton serviteur habiterait-il avec toi dans la ville royale ? »
fr.R: Ensuite, David a dit à Akish : « Si tu es content de moi, s’il te plaît, donne-moi un endroit dans une des villes de la campagne. Je pourrai y vivre. Ce n’est pas la peine que j’habite avec toi dans la ville du roi. »

vi.L: Đa-vít nói với A-kích: "Nếu tôi được ơn trước mắt vua, xin cho tôi một chỗ trong một thành ở thôn quê, để tôi ở đó. Vì sao đầy tớ của vua lại ở trong kinh thành với vua?"
vi.B: Rồi Đa-vít thưa với A-kích: "Nếu bệ hạ đoái thương, xin cho tôi một chỗ ở trong một thị trấn ngoài thôn quê để tôi sống ở đó. Sao đầy tớ của bệ hạ lại ở trong kinh thành với bệ hạ?"
vi.R: Rồi Đa-vít thưa với A-kích: "Nếu đức vua hài lòng về tôi, xin cho tôi một chỗ ở trong một thị trấn ngoài thôn quê. Tôi có thể sống ở đó. Tôi không cần phải sống với vua trong kinh thành."

decisions.choice: found favor in your eyes: if you are pleased with me
decisions.reason: A polite way of asking a favor of someone of higher rank (20:29; Genesis 18:3).

decisions.choice: towns of the field: country towns
decisions.reason: "The field" is the open country, away from the capital. David asks for a town of his own at a distance from Gath.

decisions.choice: your servant ... the royal city: a humble request with a hidden purpose
decisions.reason: David speaks of himself as "your servant", a polite way of saying "me", and makes it sound as if he is too lowly to live in the king's city. Away from Achish's eyes he will be free to act as he pleases, as verses 8-12 show.

decisions.choice: There is no need for me to live with you in the king's city.
decisions.reason: Readable turns David's question into the statement it implies and says "me" for the polite "your servant".

decisions.choice: David speaks to Achish as a subject to a king: "vua" / "bệ hạ" / "đức vua", and "đầy tớ của vua" (L, B), "tôi" (R); Achish says "ta" and "ngươi"
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note for subjects and the king; David now serves the king of Gath (m3), and keeps these forms through chapters 27-29.

source.text: וַיִּתֶּן־ל֥וֹ אָכִ֛ישׁ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא אֶת־צִֽקְלָ֑ג לָכֵ֞ן הָיְתָ֤ה צִֽקְלַג֙ לְמַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And gave to him Achish on the day the that Ziklag; therefore has belonged Ziklag to [the] kings of Judah until the day the this.

en.L: And Achish gave him Ziklag on that day; therefore Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah to this day.
en.B: So that day Achish gave him Ziklag. That is why Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah to this day.
en.R: So that day Achish gave David the town of Ziklag. That is why Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah to this day.

es.L: Y le dio Aquis aquel día Siclag; por eso Siclag ha pertenecido a los reyes de Judá hasta el día de hoy.
es.B: Así que aquel día Aquis le dio Siclag. Por eso Siclag ha pertenecido a los reyes de Judá hasta el día de hoy.
es.R: Así que aquel día Aquis le dio a David el pueblo de Siclag. Por eso Siclag ha pertenecido a los reyes de Judá hasta el día de hoy.

fr.L: Et Akish lui donna ce jour-là Tsiqlag ; c’est pourquoi Tsiqlag a appartenu aux rois de Juda jusqu’à ce jour.
fr.B: Ce jour-là, Akish lui donna donc Tsiqlag. C’est pourquoi Tsiqlag appartient aux rois de Juda jusqu’à aujourd’hui.
fr.R: Ce jour-là, Akish a donc donné à David la ville de Tsiqlag. C’est pour cela que Tsiqlag appartient aux rois de Juda jusqu’à aujourd’hui.

vi.L: Ngày hôm đó A-kích cho ông Xiếc-lác; vì vậy Xiếc-lác thuộc về các vua Giu-đa cho đến ngày nay.
vi.B: Vậy hôm đó A-kích ban cho ông thành Xiếc-lác. Vì thế Xiếc-lác thuộc về các vua Giu-đa cho đến ngày nay.
vi.R: Vậy hôm đó A-kích ban cho Đa-vít thành Xiếc-lác. Vì thế Xiếc-lác thuộc về các vua Giu-đa cho đến ngày nay.

decisions.choice: Ziklag: a town in the far south
decisions.reason: Ziklag lay in the south of the land, toward the Negev. It had been listed among the towns of Judah and of Simeon (Joshua 15:31; 19:5), but it was then in Philistine hands. From here David could raid the desert peoples to the south (verse 8).

decisions.choice: to this day: up to the writer's own time
decisions.reason: As in 5:5, the phrase refers to the time when the book was written. "The kings of Judah" suggests a writer who knew the line of David's descendants who reigned in Judah, long after these events.

decisions.choice: the town of Ziklag
decisions.reason: Readable adds "the town of" so that the unfamiliar name is clear, and names David for "him".

decisions.choice: hasta el día de hoy
decisions.reason: “To this day” is the writer's own day (m2), as the Samuel terms note sets; the same words at every level. Recorded once for this block.

source.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ מִסְפַּ֣ר הַיָּמִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־יָשַׁ֥ב דָּוִ֖ד בִּשְׂדֵ֣ה פְלִשְׁתִּ֑ים יָמִ֖ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֥ה חֳדָשִֽׁים׃

records.literal_gloss: And was the number of the days which dwelt David in [the] field of [the] Philistines days and four months.

en.L: And the number of the days that David dwelt in the country of the Philistines was days and four months.
en.B: David lived in Philistine territory for a year and four months.
en.R: David lived in the land of the Philistines for a year and four months.

es.L: Y fue el número de los días que David habitó en el campo de los filisteos días y cuatro meses.
es.B: David vivió en territorio filisteo un año y cuatro meses.
es.R: David vivió en la tierra de los filisteos un año y cuatro meses.

fr.L: Et le nombre des jours que David habita dans la campagne des Philistins fut des jours et quatre mois.
fr.B: David vécut en territoire philistin un an et quatre mois.
fr.R: David a vécu dans le pays des Philistins pendant un an et quatre mois.

vi.L: Số ngày Đa-vít ở trong xứ của người Phi-li-tin là [một số] ngày và bốn tháng.
vi.B: Đa-vít sống trong lãnh thổ người Phi-li-tin một năm bốn tháng.
vi.R: Đa-vít sống trong xứ của người Phi-li-tin một năm bốn tháng.

decisions.choice: days: a year
decisions.reason: "Days" can stand for a full year, as in 1:3 and 2:19, where "from days to days" means every year, and Judges 17:10. So the time is a year and four months. The early Greek translation has only "four months".

decisions.choice: the field of the Philistines: the Philistines' country
decisions.reason: "Field" here means territory or region (also verse 11).

decisions.choice: a year and four months
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "days"; Balanced and Readable give the sense explained in the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: días y cuatro meses (L); un año y cuatro meses (B, R)
alternatives: un año y cuatro meses at every level
decisions.reason: “Days” here means a full year (m1). Literal keeps the Hebrew word, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable say “un año” (r-en-1).

source.text: וַיַּ֤עַל דָּוִד֙ וַֽאֲנָשָׁ֔יו וַֽיִּפְשְׁט֛וּ אֶל־הַגְּשׁוּרִ֥י וְהַגִּזְרִ֖י וְהָעֲמָלֵקִ֑י כִּ֣י הֵ֜נָּה יֹשְׁב֤וֹת הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מֵֽעוֹלָ֔ם בּוֹאֲךָ֥ שׁ֖וּרָה וְעַד־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And went up David and his men and they raided against the Geshurite[s] and the Gizrite[s] and the Amalekite[s], for they [were] dwelling [in] the land which [was] from of old, your coming toward Shur and as far as [the] land of Egypt.

en.L: And David and his men went up and raided the Geshurites and the Gizrites and the Amalekites, for they [were] the inhabitants of the land from of old, as you go toward Shur and as far as the land of Egypt.
en.B: David and his men would go up and raid the Geshurites, the Gizrites and the Amalekites. These peoples had lived in the land from ancient times, in the region that stretches toward Shur and on to the land of Egypt.
en.R: David and his men would go out and attack the Geshurites, the Gizrites and the Amalekites. These peoples had lived for a very long time in the land that reaches toward the desert of Shur and as far as Egypt.

es.L: Y subieron David y sus hombres e hicieron incursiones contra los gesureos, los gezritas y los amalecitas, porque ellos [eran] los habitantes de la tierra desde antiguo, en dirección a Shur y hasta la tierra de Egipto.
es.B: David y sus hombres subían a hacer incursiones contra los gesureos, los gezritas y los amalecitas. Estos pueblos habitaban la región desde tiempos antiguos, en la zona que se extiende hacia Shur y hasta la tierra de Egipto.
es.R: David y sus hombres salían a atacar a los gesureos, los gezritas y los amalecitas. Estos pueblos habían vivido desde hacía mucho tiempo en la tierra que llega hasta el desierto de Shur y hasta Egipto.

fr.L: Et David et ses hommes montèrent et firent des incursions chez les Gueshourites, les Guizrites et les Amalécites, car ils [étaient] les habitants du pays depuis toujours, du côté de Shour et jusqu’au pays d’Égypte.
fr.B: David et ses hommes montaient faire des incursions chez les Gueshourites, les Guizrites et les Amalécites. Ces peuples habitaient le pays depuis les temps anciens, dans la région qui s’étend vers Shour et jusqu’au pays d’Égypte.
fr.R: David et ses hommes partaient attaquer les Gueshourites, les Guizrites et les Amalécites. Ces peuples habitaient depuis très longtemps la région qui va vers le désert de Shour et jusqu’à l’Égypte.

vi.L: Đa-vít và những người của ông đi lên đột kích người Ghê-su-rơ, người Ghiệt-xi và người A-ma-léc, vì họ là dân cư của xứ từ xưa, khi đi về phía Su-rơ cho đến xứ Ai Cập.
vi.B: Đa-vít và thuộc hạ thường đi lên đột kích người Ghê-su-rơ, người Ghiệt-xi và người A-ma-léc. Những dân này đã sống trong xứ từ thời xa xưa, trong vùng trải dài về phía Su-rơ cho đến xứ Ai Cập.
vi.R: Đa-vít và thuộc hạ thường đi tấn công người Ghê-su-rơ, người Ghiệt-xi và người A-ma-léc. Những dân này đã sống từ rất lâu trong vùng đất trải dài đến hoang mạc Su-rơ và đến tận Ai Cập.

decisions.choice: Geshurites, Gizrites, Amalekites: desert peoples of the south
decisions.reason: These were peoples living in the dry south between Philistia and Egypt. These Geshurites are the southern ones of Joshua 13:2, not the Geshur north-east of Galilee. The Amalekites were Israel's old enemies (Exodus 17:8-16; 15:2-3).

decisions.choice: the Gizrites: the reading noted in the margin
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text spell the name "Girzites", and the reading noted by the scribes in the margin has "Gizrites", which may mean people linked with the town of Gezer. The name is known only here, so it is uncertain which form is original.

decisions.choice: from of old: the land they had lived in for ages
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "from of old" says these peoples had long lived there. Some copies of the early Greek translation read a place name, "from Telam" (compare Telaim in 15:4). The Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: toward Shur, as far as Egypt: the same region as 15:7
decisions.reason: Shur was the desert east of Egypt (Genesis 16:7; Exodus 15:22). Saul struck the Amalekites "from Havilah toward Shur, which is east of Egypt" (15:7), yet Amalekites still live there, and they return in chapter 30.

decisions.choice: went up and raided: the first of many raids
decisions.reason: Verses 8-11 describe what David did again and again during his time at Ziklag; verse 11 says this was "his practice". This verse tells the raids as one story, and the next verses use forms for repeated action.

decisions.choice: would go up and raid
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "would" to show that these raids happened many times, as verses 9-11 make plain.

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal ("montèrent"); imparfait at Balanced and Readable ("montaient", "partaient")
decisions.reason: Verses 8-11 tell what David did again and again (m5); as the English Balanced and Readable say "would", French uses the imparfait of repeated action there, and in verses 9-11 at every level.

decisions.choice: les Gueshourites, les Guizrites, Shour
decisions.reason: Names not in the terms table, in the usual French transcription; the Amalécites as the Samuel terms note sets.

decisions.choice: los gesureos, los gezritas, los amalecitas
decisions.reason: The usual Spanish forms of these desert peoples (m1); the Gizrites follow the margin's reading (m2), as the English does.

decisions.choice: "người Ghê-su-rơ", "người Ghiệt-xi", "người A-ma-léc", "Su-rơ"
decisions.reason: "người A-ma-léc" as the terms note, "Su-rơ" as the Vietnamese Genesis; the other two peoples take the usual Protestant forms.

source.text: וְהִכָּ֤ה דָוִד֙ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְלֹ֥א יְחַיֶּ֖ה אִ֣ישׁ וְאִשָּׁ֑ה וְלָקַח֩ צֹ֨אן וּבָקָ֜ר וַחֲמֹרִ֤ים וּגְמַלִּים֙ וּבְגָדִ֔ים וַיָּ֖שָׁב וַיָּבֹ֥א אֶל־אָכִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And would strike David the land, and not he would let live man and woman, and he would take sheep and cattle and donkeys and camels and clothes, and he returned and came to Achish.

en.L: And David would strike the land and would not let man or woman live, and he would take sheep and cattle and donkeys and camels and clothing, and he returned and came to Achish.
en.B: Whenever David attacked the region, he left no man or woman alive. He took the sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels and clothing, and then came back to Achish.
en.R: Each time David attacked an area, he killed every man and woman. He took their sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels and clothes. Then he went back to Achish.

es.L: Y hería David la tierra, y no dejaba con vida hombre ni mujer, y tomaba ovejas, vacas, asnos, camellos y ropa, y volvía y venía a Aquis.
es.B: Cada vez que David atacaba la región, no dejaba con vida a ningún hombre ni a ninguna mujer. Se llevaba las ovejas, las vacas, los asnos, los camellos y la ropa, y luego volvía a donde estaba Aquis.
es.R: Cada vez que David atacaba una región, mataba a todos los hombres y mujeres. Se llevaba sus ovejas, vacas, burros, camellos y ropa. Después volvía a donde estaba Aquis.

fr.L: Et David frappait le pays, et il ne laissait vivre ni homme ni femme, et il prenait moutons et bœufs, et ânes et chameaux, et vêtements, et il revenait et rentrait chez Akish.
fr.B: Chaque fois que David attaquait la région, il ne laissait en vie ni homme ni femme. Il prenait les moutons, les bœufs, les ânes, les chameaux et les vêtements, puis il revenait chez Akish.
fr.R: Chaque fois que David attaquait une région, il tuait tous les hommes et toutes les femmes. Il prenait leurs moutons, leurs bœufs, leurs ânes, leurs chameaux et leurs vêtements. Ensuite, il retournait chez Akish.

vi.L: Đa-vít đánh xứ ấy và không để người nam hay người nữ nào sống sót; ông lấy chiên, bò, lừa, lạc đà và quần áo, rồi trở về đến với A-kích.
vi.B: Mỗi lần Đa-vít tấn công vùng nào, ông không để một người nam hay người nữ nào sống sót. Ông lấy chiên, bò, lừa, lạc đà và quần áo, rồi trở về với A-kích.
vi.R: Mỗi lần Đa-vít tấn công một vùng nào, ông giết hết đàn ông và đàn bà. Ông lấy chiên, bò, lừa, lạc đà và quần áo của họ. Rồi ông trở về với A-kích.

decisions.choice: would strike ... would not let live ... would take: repeated action
decisions.reason: The verbs are in a form that describes what happened again and again, so this is what David did on every raid, not on one occasion.

decisions.choice: not letting man or woman live: so that no one could report
decisions.reason: Verse 11 gives the reason: no survivor must reach Gath to tell what David was really doing. The story reports this plainly; it does not say God commanded it.

decisions.choice: sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, clothing: the plunder
decisions.reason: These were the wealth of desert herding peoples. David brings the plunder back, and Achish presumably receives a share as his overlord (compare 30:26).

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אָכִ֔ישׁ אַל־פְּשַׁטְתֶּ֖ם הַיּ֑וֹם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗ד עַל־נֶ֤גֶב יְהוּדָה֙ וְעַל־נֶ֣גֶב הַיַּרְחְמְאֵלִ֔י וְאֶל־נֶ֖גֶב הַקֵּינִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And would say Achish, Not have you raided the day? And would say David, Against [the] Negev of Judah, and against [the] Negev of the Jerahmeelite[s], and against [the] Negev of the Kenite[s].

en.L: And Achish would say, "Have you not raided today?" And David would say, "Against the Negev of Judah," or "Against the Negev of the Jerahmeelites," or "Against the Negev of the Kenites."
en.B: When Achish asked, "Did you not go raiding today?" David would answer, "Against the Negev of Judah," or "Against the Negev of the Jerahmeelites," or "Against the Negev of the Kenites."
en.R: Achish would ask him, "You went raiding today, did you not?" David would answer, "Yes, against the southern part of Judah." Or he would say, "Against the south, where the Jerahmeelites live," or "Against the south, where the Kenites live."

es.L: Y decía Aquis: «¿No han hecho incursión hoy?». Y decía David: «Contra el Néguev de Judá», o «Contra el Néguev de los jerameelitas», o «Contra el Néguev de los ceneos».
es.B: Cuando Aquis le preguntaba: «¿No saliste hoy de incursión?», David respondía: «Contra el Néguev de Judá», o «Contra el Néguev de los jerameelitas», o «Contra el Néguev de los ceneos».
es.R: Aquis le preguntaba: «Hoy saliste a atacar, ¿verdad?». David le contestaba: «Sí, contra el sur de Judá». O le decía: «Contra el sur, donde viven los jerameelitas», o «Contra el sur, donde viven los ceneos».

fr.L: Et Akish disait : « N’avez-vous pas fait d’incursion aujourd’hui ? » Et David disait : « Contre le Néguev de Juda », ou « Contre le Néguev des Yerahméelites », ou « Contre le Néguev des Kéniens ».
fr.B: Quand Akish demandait : « N’êtes-vous pas allés faire une incursion aujourd’hui ? », David répondait : « Contre le Néguev de Juda », ou « Contre le Néguev des Yerahméelites », ou « Contre le Néguev des Kéniens ».
fr.R: Akish lui demandait : « Vous êtes allés attaquer quelque part aujourd’hui, non ? » David répondait : « Oui, dans le sud de Juda. » Ou bien il disait : « Dans le sud, là où vivent les Yerahméelites », ou : « Dans le sud, là où vivent les Kéniens. »

vi.L: A-kích hỏi: "Hôm nay ngươi không đi đột kích sao?" Đa-vít đáp: "Đánh miền Nê-ghép của Giu-đa," hoặc "Đánh miền Nê-ghép của người Giê-rác-mê-ên," hoặc "Đánh miền Nê-ghép của người Kê-nít."
vi.B: Khi A-kích hỏi: "Hôm nay ngươi không đi đột kích sao?" Đa-vít đáp: "Đánh miền Nê-ghép của Giu-đa," hoặc "Đánh miền Nê-ghép của người Giê-rác-mê-ên," hoặc "Đánh miền Nê-ghép của người Kê-nít."
vi.R: A-kích hỏi ông: "Hôm nay ngươi đi đột kích phải không?" Đa-vít đáp: "Vâng, đánh miền nam Giu-đa." Hoặc ông nói: "Đánh miền nam, nơi người Giê-rác-mê-ên sống," hay "Đánh miền nam, nơi người Kê-nít sống."

decisions.choice: Have you not raided today?: the Hebrew as it stands
alternatives: Against whom did you raid today?
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has the word for "not", making a question that expects the answer "yes". The early Greek translation reads "Against whom did you raid today?", which fits David's answers well and may reflect a slightly different Hebrew word. The Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: Judah, the Jerahmeelites, the Kenites: David's own people and their friends
decisions.reason: The Negev is the dry south. The Jerahmeelites were a clan of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:9, 25), and the Kenites were friends of Israel who lived among Judah (15:6; Judges 1:16). David names Israel's own south to make Achish believe he is attacking his own people (verse 12). In truth he raided Israel's enemies (verse 8).

decisions.choice: would say: a repeated exchange
decisions.reason: Like verse 9, this describes what happened after each raid. David gave one of these answers each time.

decisions.choice: Yes; the southern part of Judah; where the Jerahmeelites live
decisions.reason: Readable adds "Yes" to show that Achish's question expects it, and explains "Negev" as the south and the clan names as the people living there.

decisions.choice: le Néguev; les Yerahméelites, les Kéniens
decisions.reason: The Negev keeps its name at Literal and Balanced, as the English; Readable says "le sud". Les Kéniens as the Samuel terms note sets.

decisions.choice: «¿No han hecho incursión hoy?» (impersonal)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew as it stands asks “Have you not raided today?” (m1); Literal leaves the subject open with an impersonal plural, which is not an address to David's men, and Balanced and Readable ask David himself, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "miền Nê-ghép" (L, B); "miền nam" (R); "người Giê-rác-mê-ên", "người Kê-nít"
decisions.reason: "Nê-ghép" as the Vietnamese Genesis; Readable says "the south" as the English Readable does.

source.text: וְאִ֨ישׁ וְאִשָּׁ֜ה לֹֽא־יְחַיֶּ֣ה דָוִ֗ד לְהָבִ֥יא גַת֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר פֶּן־יַגִּ֥דוּ עָלֵ֖ינוּ לֵאמֹ֑ר כֹּֽה־עָשָׂ֤ה דָוִד֙ וְכֹ֣ה מִשְׁפָּט֔וֹ כָּל־הַ֨יָּמִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָשַׁ֖ב בִּשְׂדֵ֥ה פְלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And man and woman not would let live David to bring [to] Gath, saying, Lest they tell about us, saying, Thus has done David. And thus [was] his practice all the days which he dwelt in [the] field of [the] Philistines.

en.L: And David would not let man or woman live to bring [them to] Gath, saying, "Lest they tell about us, saying, 'Thus David has done.'" And thus [was] his practice all the days that he dwelt in the country of the Philistines.
en.B: David left no man or woman alive to bring to Gath, for he thought, "They might report on us and say, 'This is what David did.'" This was his practice the whole time he lived in Philistine territory.
en.R: David did not leave any man or woman alive to be brought back to Gath. He thought, "They might tell what we did. They would say, 'This is what David has been doing.'" David did this the whole time he lived in the land of the Philistines.

es.L: Y no dejaba David con vida hombre ni mujer para traer[los a] Gat, diciendo: «No sea que hablen contra nosotros, diciendo: “Así hizo David”». Y así [fue] su costumbre todos los días que habitó en el campo de los filisteos.
es.B: David no dejaba con vida a ningún hombre ni mujer para llevarlos a Gat, porque pensaba: «Podrían delatarnos y decir: “Esto es lo que hizo David”». Esa fue su costumbre todo el tiempo que vivió en territorio filisteo.
es.R: David no dejaba con vida a ningún hombre ni a ninguna mujer para llevarlos a Gat. Pensaba: «Podrían contar lo que hicimos. Dirían: “Esto es lo que David ha estado haciendo”». David hizo esto todo el tiempo que vivió en la tierra de los filisteos.

fr.L: Et David ne laissait vivre ni homme ni femme pour [les] amener à Gath, se disant : « De peur qu’ils ne racontent sur nous, en disant : “Voilà ce qu’a fait David.” » Et telle [fut] sa manière d’agir pendant tout le temps qu’il habita dans la campagne des Philistins.
fr.B: David ne laissait en vie ni homme ni femme qu’on aurait pu amener à Gath, car il pensait : « Ils pourraient faire un rapport contre nous et dire : “Voilà ce que David a fait.” » Telle fut sa façon d’agir pendant tout le temps qu’il vécut en territoire philistin.
fr.R: David ne laissait aucun homme et aucune femme en vie pour qu’on les ramène à Gath. Il pensait : « Ils pourraient raconter ce que nous avons fait. Ils diraient : “Voilà ce que David fait.” » David a agi ainsi pendant tout le temps où il a vécu dans le pays des Philistins.

vi.L: Đa-vít không để người nam hay người nữ nào sống để đem [về] Gát, vì ông nói: "Kẻo họ nói về chúng ta rằng: 'Đa-vít đã làm như thế.'" Đó [là] cách ông làm suốt những ngày ông ở trong xứ của người Phi-li-tin.
vi.B: Đa-vít không để một người nam hay người nữ nào sống sót để đem về Gát, vì ông nghĩ: "Họ có thể tố cáo chúng ta và nói: 'Đa-vít đã làm như thế.'" Ông làm như vậy suốt thời gian sống trong lãnh thổ người Phi-li-tin.
vi.R: Đa-vít không để một người đàn ông hay đàn bà nào sống sót để đem về Gát. Ông nghĩ: "Họ có thể kể lại những gì chúng ta đã làm. Họ sẽ nói: 'Đa-vít đã làm những việc như thế.'" Đa-vít làm như vậy suốt thời gian sống trong xứ của người Phi-li-tin.

decisions.choice: saying: David's reason, in his own thoughts
decisions.reason: "Saying" here introduces what David had in mind, his reason for leaving no survivors, not words spoken aloud.

decisions.choice: and such was his practice: the narrator's words
alternatives: part of what the survivors would report
decisions.reason: The last clause could still belong to what the survivors might report ("this is what David did, and this was his way the whole time"). It is read here as the narrator's own summary, closing the account of the raids that began in verse 8.

decisions.choice: his practice: his custom, his way of doing things
decisions.reason: The word usually means a ruling or judgment, but it can also mean a custom or usual way (2:13; 8:9). Here it is David's regular way of acting.

decisions.choice: he thought ... They might report on us
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable express "lest" as "might" and make clear that this was David's thinking.

source.text: וַיַּאֲמֵ֥ן אָכִ֖ישׁ בְּדָוִ֣ד לֵאמֹ֑ר הַבְאֵ֤שׁ הִבְאִישׁ֙ בְּעַמּ֣וֹ בְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְהָ֥יָה לִ֖י לְעֶ֥בֶד עוֹלָֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And trusted Achish in David, saying, He has surely made himself stink among his people, in Israel, and he will be to me [a] slave forever.

en.L: And Achish trusted David, saying, "He has surely made himself a stench among his people, in Israel, and he will be my slave forever."
en.B: Achish trusted David and thought, "He has made himself utterly hated by his own people, the Israelites, so he will be my servant for life."
en.R: Achish believed David. He thought, "David has made his own people, the Israelites, hate him completely. So he will have to serve me for the rest of his life."

es.L: Y Aquis confiaba en David, diciendo: «Ciertamente se ha hecho odioso a su pueblo, a Israel, y será mi esclavo para siempre».
es.B: Aquis confiaba en David, y pensaba: «Se ha hecho aborrecible para su propio pueblo, los israelitas, así que será mi siervo para toda la vida».
es.R: Aquis le creía a David. Pensaba: «David ha hecho que los israelitas, su propio pueblo, lo odien por completo. Así que tendrá que servirme el resto de su vida».

fr.L: Et Akish eut confiance en David, se disant : « Il s’est vraiment rendu odieux à son peuple, à Israël, et il sera mon esclave pour toujours. »
fr.B: Akish avait confiance en David et pensait : « Il s’est rendu complètement odieux à son propre peuple, les Israélites ; il sera donc mon serviteur à vie. »
fr.R: Akish a cru David. Il pensait : « David s’est fait détester complètement par son propre peuple, les Israélites. Alors il devra me servir pour le reste de sa vie. »

vi.L: A-kích tin Đa-vít và nói: "Hắn chắc chắn đã làm cho mình thành mùi hôi thối giữa dân mình, trong Y-sơ-ra-ên, và hắn sẽ làm nô lệ cho ta mãi mãi."
vi.B: A-kích tin Đa-vít và nghĩ: "Hắn đã làm cho dân mình, là người Y-sơ-ra-ên, ghét cay ghét đắng, nên hắn sẽ làm đầy tớ cho ta suốt đời."
vi.R: A-kích tin Đa-vít. Vua nghĩ: "Đa-vít đã làm cho chính dân mình, là người Y-sơ-ra-ên, căm ghét hắn hoàn toàn. Vì vậy hắn sẽ phải phục vụ ta suốt đời."

decisions.choice: made himself a stench: made himself hated
decisions.reason: The verb means to stink. To make oneself a stench to someone is to make them loathe you (13:4; 2 Samuel 10:6). The verb is doubled for emphasis: Achish thinks David's own people now utterly loathe him.

decisions.choice: a slave forever: bound to serve for life
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of a slave who stays with his master for life (Deuteronomy 15:17; Exodus 21:6). Achish thinks David can never go home, so he must be loyal to Achish for good. David is in fact deceiving him, and the reader sees the irony (29:6-9).

decisions.choice: saying: what Achish thought
decisions.reason: As in verse 11, "saying" introduces a person's thoughts. Achish does not say this to David.

decisions.choice: servant (Balanced); serve me (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "slave"; Balanced and Readable say "servant" and "serve", following the usual rule for this word. The meaning decision keeps the sense of lifelong bondage.

decisions.choice: se ha hecho odioso (L); aborrecible (B)
decisions.reason: “Made himself a stench” means made himself hated (m1). A literal “hediondo” would read oddly in Spanish, so even Literal gives the sense, as the English Readable does.
